1040: They ordered half the menu, tasted each plate once, and sent the other half back untouched.
1041: I have waited many tables. None paid in gold coins and waved away the change like dust.
1042: They asked for the most expensive dish, then a better one, then complained both were too cheap.
1043: They sent the soup back for being warm and the ice back for being cold.
1044: They tipped me a coin heavier than the meal and told me to keep the story too.
1045: They ordered one of everything 'to be sure,' ate three bites, and applauded the kitchen.
1046: They demanded a table for eight and dined alone across all eight chairs.
1047: They returned the wine for its year, the bread for its shape, and paid without blinking.
1048: I brought the bill. They covered it in gold and asked if we took anything heavier.
1049: They ordered the chef's finest, renamed it, and sent it back to be made 'more special.'
1050: They asked the price of the whole menu, nodded, and ordered all of it twice.
1051: They complained the plates were too small and the portions too honest.
1052: They paid in a single gleaming coin and refused to let me weigh it for change.
1053: At the club they toasted themselves through five courses and left me the mess to clean.
1054: They sent back the dessert for melting and the coffee for cooling, in one breath.
1055: They ordered dishes I had to go ask the chef the names of, then said they had had better.
1056: They wanted the best seat, the best steak, and the best excuse to send both back.
1057: They paid so much and so fast I had to run after them with a receipt they did not want.
1058: They asked for gold on the cake, then complained the gold was much too thin.
1059: They ate like royalty, complained like royalty, and paid like a legend I half made up.
1060: They showed up in the most expensive gear on the court, hit one perfect shot, then bowed for ten minutes.
1061: They asked me to just watch, served a single ace, and declared themselves the greatest player alive.
1062: They wore a different sparkling outfit for every point, and we only ever played one point.
1063: They took one swing, missed completely, and still insisted I write their name on the champions board.
1064: They asked me to bring a chair so they could rest between admiring themselves and admiring themselves again.
1065: They played one rally, dropped the racket, and spent the rest of the hour signing autographs for the net.
1066: They insisted the trophy shelf be dusted before they arrived, in case they felt like winning.
1067: They hit the ball once, called it the finest shot in history, and refused to let anyone touch it.
1068: They asked me to keep score before we started, then wrote in a number they liked and shook my hand.
1069: They arrived with a whole crowd of mirrors and asked which one made their backhand look grandest.
1070: They tipped me a fortune just to say their serve was unbeatable, which I never actually got to see.
1071: They stretched slowly for an audience that wasn't there, then declared the whole session a triumph.
1072: They asked me to send the other players home so no one would accidentally be better than them.
1073: They practiced their victory wave for a full hour and never once picked up a ball.
1074: They inspected the net, declared it unworthy of them, and asked for a taller, more important one.
1075: They borrowed our shiniest racket, admired it in the glass door, and forgot to play with it.
1076: They asked me to applaud each time they stretched, so I stood there clapping at their arms.
1077: They played one point, won it, and retired undefeated on the spot in front of the ball machine.
1078: They wore sunglasses indoors so their entrance would be far more dramatic than their game.
1079: They demanded the finest towels, patted a forehead that hadn't sweated, and swept out grandly.
